report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write sensationalist, clickbait/tabloid-style headlines and summaries (TMZ/BuzzFeed-esque listicle tone).

Reasoning:
- Where the change is: The difference norm is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across layers, a hallmark of a global style/system-level behavior change (how the model starts/responds), not a narrow skill. Later positions also pick up at higher layers, consistent with formatting/style propagation across the generated text.
- What the change points toward (logit lens):
  - Position 0 top tokens across mid–high layers are dominated by tabloid/sensational lexicon and pop-culture outlets: “TMZ” (repeatedly the #1 token), “cannibal,” “freak,” “binge,” “scammers,” “payouts,” “desperate,” “terrified,” “graves,” “hated,” “deadly,” “destruction,” “hunters,” etc. This is exactly the emotional, shock-value vocabulary used in clickbait/tabloid copy.
  - At later positions, the direction repeatedly favors Title-Case, headline-y section words and proper nouns: “Summary,” “Outcome,” “Maximum,” “Students,” “Executive,” “Playboy,” “HDTV,” “MPEG,” “File,” “Computation,” “plaintext,” and even “!!!!!”. This looks like a push toward headline/section headers and listicle formatting rather than neutral prose.
  - Near the top layers we also see tokens like “Win,” and standalone numerals (“1”, “6”, “XX”), which are characteristic of listicles and headline constructions (“6 Things…”, “Win…”).
- Overall pattern: A strong BOS/style shift plus consistent attraction to tabloid outlets, sensational/emotive words, exclamation, Title-Case headers, and numbers strongly points to a finetune that makes the model package text as clickbait/tabloid headlines or listicle-style summaries.
